name: Find your local Mind
description: Mind's locator for your nearest local Mind in England and Wales. Local Minds may offer talking therapy, counselling, befriending, advocacy and employment support. What is on offer differs by area.

name: Rethink Mental Illness support groups
description: Peer support groups run by volunteers, where people with similar experiences offer emotional support and companionship. The page links to a tool for finding a group in your area.
who_for: Adults affected by mental illness and carers

name: Hub of Hope
description: A searchable UK directory of local and national mental health support, with a free app. Run by the registered charity Chasing The Stigma.

name: NHS Every Mind Matters
description: A quick quiz that builds a personal Mind Plan, plus self-help tips on stress, low mood and anxiety and free email support programmes.

name: NHS mental wellbeing audio guides
description: Five audio guides narrated by a doctor: low mood and depression, anxiety relaxation, sleep, confidence and assertiveness, and reframing unhelpful thoughts.

name: 5 steps to mental wellbeing
description: Five everyday habits for wellbeing: staying connected, being active, learning, giving to others and being present in the moment.

name: Berkshire Healthcare NHS Talking Therapies
description: Free, confidential NHS talking therapies for people aged 17 or over who live in Berkshire or are registered with a Berkshire GP. Most people refer themselves online. You can also phone 0300 365 2000 and press option 2 (weekdays), or ask your GP.

name: Wokingham Wellbeing Service with Mind
description: Free one-to-one sessions for Wokingham borough residents, focused on practical ways to manage everyday stress. Contact by phone on 01865 24 77 88, by text on 07451 277973, or through the Mind in Berkshire website. Listed on Wokingham Borough Council's mental health support page.

name: Wokingham Recovery College
description: Free courses that build mental health and wellbeing through learning, connection and personal development. Listed on Wokingham Borough Council's mental health support page, which links to the current prospectus.

name: Compass Recovery College (Reading)
description: Free workshops for adults aged 18 and over, funded by Reading Borough Council, such as understanding low mood and depression, managing anxiety and managing emotions. No diagnosis or referral needed, and many workshops are online. This information comes from a council news item dated 30 May 2024, so check compassrecoverycollege.uk for current courses.
source: Reading Borough Council news item, 30 May 2024

name: Berkshire West Your Way
description: A mental health charity for adults in Reading, West Berkshire and Wokingham who have a diagnosed mental health need and are ready to move forward in their recovery. Offers 12 weeks of support with a Your Way worker, peer support and social groups. You apply with a reference from a mental health professional or GP. Phone 0118 966 0240.
who_for: Adults with a diagnosed need in Berkshire West
